title: Curie's law for a paramagnet
caption: Susceptibility χ = C/T. With χ = 2 × 10⁻⁴ at 300 K, C = 0.060000000000000005 K; cooling tenfold to 30 K raises χ tenfold to 2 × 10⁻³. Thermal motion fights the alignment of moments, so the response grows as the temperature falls.
alt: Graph of susceptibility (units of 10⁻⁴) against temperature: a falling hyperbola passing through 2 at 300 K and 20 at 30 K.
description: The horizontal axis is the temperature in kelvin; the vertical axis is the susceptibility in units of 10⁻⁴.
The curve is χ = C/T with C = 0.060000000000000005 K.
At 300 K, χ = 2 × 10⁻⁴; at 30 K, χ = 20 × 10⁻⁴ = 2 × 10⁻³: ten times larger for a tenth of the temperature.
